summary.text: 着 is commonly used as the Mandarin particle zhe, marking ongoing or persistent action. Its written form is historically linked to 著, but that link does not show that 著’s other uses were also uses of 着.

formation.text: 着 is a later graph related to 著, which is traditionally analyzed as a phonosemantic compound: 艹 contributes a grass or plant category, and 者 is assigned a sound role. This analysis describes 著, not an independently established ancient construction for 着.

components.text: In 著, 艹 is analyzed as a semantic element contributing a grass or plant category. This does not identify a particular plant or establish the graph’s earliest meaning.

sound.text: The modern readings share an initial zh sound, but this resemblance does not prove an ancient relationship.

history.text: 着 is recorded in a Tang-period inscription, and later orthographic works describe it as a vulgar or erroneous writing of 著. 著 is traditionally analyzed as 艹 plus 者; its earliest surviving form and a dated sequence are not established by this evidence.

Accounts of 着’s graphic history disagree: one describes it as a copying corruption of 著, while another proposes cursive or abbreviated development. Neither provides a complete dated sequence. The Tang label 俗字 is an orthographic judgment, not an account of how the shape arose.

uncertainties.text: The precise graphic path from 著 to 着 remains unresolved. The inherited component analysis and readings of 著 do not establish an independent ancient construction for 着.
者 is traditionally assigned a sound role in 著, but the available modern and reconstructed readings do not settle the historical relationship.

evidence.source: Ministry of Education, Taiwan, Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants
evidence.field: A03506-003 research note and cited historical authorities
evidence.text: The dictionary treats 着 as an orthographic variant of 著. Its note cites a Tang inscription, the 《俗書刊誤》, 《字學三正》, and 《正字通》; the latter sources describe 着 as a俗訛 or copying error of 著. Its editors reason that 著 derives from 艸 plus 者 and that the transmitted form 着 reflects a corrupted writing of 著. This is an explicit historical orthographic analysis, not proof that every modern use of 着 is merely a copying error.
evidence.title: [A03506-003] 着 (著) — Ministry of Education Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants

evidence.text: The dictionary analyzes 著 as a phonosemantic graph from 艹 and 者, with 者 functioning as sound. It lists no ancient graphic sequence beyond later clerical forms, so this supports a traditional component analysis but does not independently establish its earliest paleographic shape. The functional reading is not identical to a claim that 艹 specifically means a particular plant in the compound.
evidence.title: 著 zhù、zhuó、zhe — 漢典

evidence.text: The dictionary distinguishes readings and senses: zhuó includes ‘put on’ and ‘attach/contact’; zhù includes ‘make manifest’ and ‘write/compose’; zhe is a grammatical particle for ongoing or persistent action. It cites the poem 《焦仲卿妻》 for 著我繡裌裙, and Tang Li Bai for 身著赤霜袍, as wear/put-on uses; it cites early-classical works for manifest/write senses. These are dictionary-attributed textual examples, not independently dated manuscript witnesses, and they do not establish a chronological semantic chain among the senses.
evidence.title: 著 zhù、zhuó、zhe — 漢典

evidence.field: 康熙字典 quotation and variant note
evidence.text: The quoted 《康熙字典》 entry gives distinct historical readings and glosses, including 陟略切 for clothing/wearing and 直略切 for placing, and says 着 is a俗 form under 土著. This establishes that later lexicography recognized multiple 著 readings and a 着 spelling, but does not itself date the origin of each sense.
evidence.title: 著 zhù、zhuó、zhe — 漢典

evidence.source: 漢字文化資料館, Taishukan Shoten
evidence.field: Q0219 historical account of 着/著
evidence.text: This account proposes that 着 arose from cursive or abbreviated writing of 著. It says 著 formerly covered both the chaku ‘wear’ reading and the cho ‘make manifest’ reading, with graphic differentiation later accompanying functional specialization. This conflicts in emphasis with the Ministry variant dictionary's transmitted-corruption account. The page does not provide dated manuscript examples or a detailed paleographic chain, so the cursive derivation remains a reported proposal rather than a demonstrated chronology.
evidence.title: Q0219: 著色 and 着色 — 漢字文化資料館

evidence.text: The dictionary gives modern Mandarin zhě, Middle Chinese 照章母 馬韻 上聲, and the traditional 《說文》 analysis ‘別事詞也。从白𣥐聲’; its displayed graphic inventory includes late Shang and Western Zhou bronze inscriptions, Chu manuscripts, Qin slips and clerical forms. This supports the component character's historical reading record, but that source's MC transcription is not a Baxter–Sagart reconstruction and should not be merged with one.
evidence.title: 者 zhě — 漢典

The editors explain the transmitted shape through the writing of 著/者 and conclude that 着 is an orthographic variant of 著. This is an explicit historical spelling analysis; it does not show that every later use of 着 was only a copying error. The entry lists image records for 《干祿字書》 and other works, but those cited images were not inspected here.
evidence.title: [A03506-003] 着 (著) — Ministry of Education Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants

evidence.source: 漢字文化資料館, Taishukan Shoten
evidence.field: Q0219 historical account of 着/著
evidence.text: This reference proposes that 着 developed from cursive or abbreviated 著. It says 著 was used both for chaku ‘put on/wear’ and cho ‘make manifest’, with graphic differentiation accompanying later functional specialization. It provides illustrative shapes but no dated manuscript chain in the text. This differs in emphasis from the Ministry dictionary’s transmitted-corruption account; neither source here establishes the full sequence and its dates.
evidence.title: Q0219: 著色 and 着色 — 漢字文化資料館

evidence.text: The dictionary describes 著 as a phonosemantic graph with 艹 as semantic element and 者 as phonetic element. It lists zhù senses including manifest/show and write/compose, zhuó senses including wear/put on, attach/contact and reach, and zhe as a continuing-action particle. Its classical citations attest examples of these uses in named works, but the list does not establish a chronological semantic chain or manuscript dates for those quotations. It says 著 is not a headword in 說文 and refers to 箸 instead.
evidence.title: 著 zhù、zhuó、zhe — 漢典

evidence.field: 者 modern reading and 說文 account
evidence.text: The entry gives modern Mandarin zhě and quotes the traditional 說文 analysis ‘別事詞也’, with a graphic analysis involving 白 and 𣥐. This confirms the traditional account and current reading; it is not a Baxter–Sagart reconstruction or independent proof of 著’s phonetic relationship.
evidence.title: 者 zhě — 漢典

evidence.source: Local structured reading data; Unicode upstream attempted

evidence.text: Exact local rows report 着 zhe, 著 zhù zhe, and 者 zhě. The character-specific official Unicode lookup pages were attempted but inaccessible through the browser, so these values are documented as local readings, not externally verified Unicode page contents. Current readings do not establish an ancient sound relationship.

evidence.source: Local structured reading data; official Baxter–Sagart supplementary site inspected
evidence.field: sources/baxter-sagart/baxtersagart.tsv rows for 者 and 著
evidence.text: The exact local Baxter–Sagart rows give 者 MC tsyaeX, OC *tAʔ, gloss ‘(nominalizing particle)’. For 著 they give zhù MC trjoH OC *t<r>ak-s ‘place (n.); visible’; zhuó MC drjak OC *m-t<r>ak ‘put on clothes; be attached’; and zhuó MC trjak OC *t<r>ak ‘to place’. The local table provides no 着 row. These readings belong to the Baxter–Sagart 2014 system; they are not compatible to silently merge with other reconstruction systems and do not alone demonstrate the phonetic role. The researchers’ official supplementary page describes its Old Chinese reconstruction materials, while the direct PDF request returned an access error.
evidence.title: The Baxter-Sagart reconstruction of Old Chinese

evidence.field: File description, original image link and licensing
evidence.text: The inspected description identifies 者-seal.svg as a digitally made vector depiction of 者 in Shuowen seal-script style and links a specific source image record. It describes the representation as public domain. The original image link was exposed on the exact description page, but the subsequent fetch failed with a cache miss. This is a modern redraw, not an ancient artifact photograph; the character is a relevant component candidate, not a direct historical form of 着.
evidence.title: File:者-seal.svg — Wikimedia Commons

context.provenance: Base evidence consists of imported local JSONL excerpts. Source names identify upstream datasets; extraction may lose sense and language boundaries. Further external evidence and research activity are documented separately in the dossier.
editorial_rules: Write about the character's graphic history; distinguish it from the history of a spoken word.
Separate historical explanation from mnemonics. Do not infer history from modern shapes or readings.
Sources may repeat one another. A source count is not independent corroboration.
Treat Shuowen as a historical account, not automatic confirmation. Its generated English glosses are excluded.
Unrelated word senses may appear in Wiktionary excerpts. Do not merge them into a character origin.
Related-character evidence retains its record_character. Do not silently transfer a traditional form's components to a simplified form.
No glyph image has been visually inspected in this packet. Do not claim to have inspected one.
Explain missing evidence explicitly, especially for Japanese-created characters. A Chinese spelling pronunciation is not evidence for a Japanese origin.

gaps: The earliest surviving graphic form of 著 and a dated sequence from ancient scripts to clerical/regular forms were not established; the accessible dictionary reports later clerical examples but no verifiable early inscriptional 著 forms.

The Ministry entry reports a Tang inscription and historical dictionary judgments, but its cited Ganlu image was not visually inspected and the actual 着 entry text was not independently transcribed here.

The cursive-derivation explanation and corruption/俗訛 explanation conflict; neither accessible account supplies a complete dated documentary chain demonstrating the transformation. Treat both as source assertions with unresolved direction/details.

The chronology linking ‘put/place’, ‘wear/attach’, ‘arrive/contact’, and the grammatical particle 着/zhe is not established by the dictionary’s gloss list or the cited examples; no semantic pathway should be asserted without further textual study.

The historical phonetic role of 者 in 著 is a conventional phonosemantic analysis. This research did not obtain comparable character-specific ancient reconstructions for both 著 and 者 within one reconstruction system, and modern/current readings cannot establish that ancient relation.

The provided local Unihan rows give modern readings for 着 and 著, but Unicode character-specific pages were inaccessible. No row for 者 was provided locally; no external character-specific Unihan reading was verified.
No reuse/license review was undertaken for recurring external references; no bulk extract is recommended from this evidence set.

No earliest surviving graphic form of 著 or dated sequence from ancient scripts through clerical and regular forms was established. The inspected authorities state 著 is absent from 說文; no reliable early inscriptional sequence was found.
The Ministry variant entry cites an image for the Tang 《干祿字書》 record, but that image was not inspected. Its actual entry text and graphic details remain unverified here.
The cursive-abbreviation account and the transmitted-corruption/俗訛 account are competing source analyses. Neither inspected source demonstrates a complete dated transformation chain.

Dictionary-attested senses include manifest/show, write/record, place, wear, attach/contact, arrive, and grammatical particle uses. Their chronological development and semantic links are unresolved; a gloss list does not establish a chain.

The phonetic role of 者 in 著 is a standard dictionary analysis, but this research did not establish an independently dated ancient sound comparison or reconstruct the earlier spoken forms behind the senses. The exact local Baxter–Sagart comparison is 著 *t<r>ak(-s) against 者 *tAʔ; role remains a dictionary source assertion, not a deduction from current Mandarin readings.
Official Unicode character-specific pages for U+7740, U+8457, and U+8005 were inaccessible. Local Unihan rows were checked but are not externally verified by those URLs.

The Commons candidate is a modern vector redraw in a seal-script style, not a historical artifact image. Its exact original image URL was obtained from the verified page, but the fetch failed; the candidate is therefore not selected as a glyph image.

limitations.text: The available evidence does not establish a verifiable historical glyph image for 着 or 著. The Tang-period record is reported, but its cited image was not inspected; accounts of cursive development and copying corruption disagree and provide no complete dated sequence. The inspected 者 image is a modern seal-script-style redraw of a component, not a historical form of either character.
